The paper proves a consistency result for the transformed objective and shows how group-centering cancels partition-function terms, allowing sampling from the student or previous student policy without importance-sampling correction. The theory is author-reported; this activation did not audit proofs, experiments or code, and does not establish training gains in practice.

item.title: OpenMAS-GCom reports controlled diagnosis of multi-agent system components
item.description: An arXiv paper introduces OpenMAS-GCom, a benchmark that compares multi-agent configurations with one component changed while tasks, models, prompts and budget limits are held fixed. The paper reports 17 configurations across 29 datasets in six domains, four interventions, and 400 frozen multi-document tasks requiring source-aware conflict resolution. In a five-dataset aggregate, it reports a 3.58 percentage-point mean score loss after specialist removal versus 0.58 points after critic removal. These are author-reported benchmark results; independent reproduction and broader task-weighted interpretation remain open.

item.title: A production-agent study compares lower-cost recurring evaluation methods
item.description: A September 2026 paper reports a temporal holdout study of partial evaluation for one production analytics agent: 574 runs of a 519-question benchmark were split evenly between calibration and held-out periods. It compares random sampling, historical caching, fixed subsets and adaptive testing. At 200 executed questions, the paper reports 1.37 percentage points of pass-rate mean absolute error in its results section, while its abstract reports 1.03 points for that budget. Difficulty-stratified fixed subsets were deployed for simplicity and tested on five additional agent families. These are author-reported results from one organization and task; the paper does not establish broad external reliability.

item.title: European Commission publishes an AI Act harmonized-standards decision for high-risk systems
item.description: The European Commission’s official AI standards index lists Implementing Decision (EU) 2026/2274, adopted on October 12 and published in the Official Journal on October 14, as concerning harmonized standards for high-risk AI systems under Regulation (EU) 2024/1689. This is a current step in the Act’s standards process. The linked legal text could not be retrieved in this review, so the specific standard references and detailed requirements remain unverified; no provider adoption or compliance outcome is established.

item.title: Insilico announces generative-biology model partnership with an unnamed frontier lab
item.description: In a Simplified Chinese issuer-distributed release dated September 21, Insilico Medicine announced a tens-of-millions USD agreement with an unnamed frontier foundation-model lab. The companies said they would combine the partner’s model architecture with Insilico’s MMAI Gym training framework and proprietary science data, conduct wet-lab validation, and pursue commercialization with revenue sharing. The announcement does not identify the counterparty or report a resulting model, measured biological outcome or realized revenue.

item.title: GestureFAR reports real-time continuous-latent streaming gestures on BEAT2
item.description: A September 18 preprint proposes token-causal co-speech gesture generation using continuous motion latents and a flow-matching head, then distills only that head to one step while freezing the causal backbone. On BEAT2, the authors report a 3.08 FGD one-step student at 9.3 ms/token, compared with 3.17 at 24.4 ms/token for their eight-step teacher, and 0.246 real-time factor on a MacBook Air. These are author-reported results for a specialized avatar/embodied-agent benchmark; no independent reproduction or deployment transfer is established.

item.title: Peng Cheng Laboratory reports PEGA-SUS1 launch with integrated satellite AI and 5G NTN payloads
item.description: Peng Cheng Laboratory's Chinese report dated Sep 20, 2026 says its PEGA-SUS1 satellite entered its planned orbit after launch aboard a Lijian-1 Y18 rocket. The lab describes the satellite as integrating a 5G non-terrestrial-network base station and core network, onboard AI compute, laser communications and microwave communications into an orbital technology-validation platform. The report says in-orbit tests, including a planned 100 Gbps laser-communications experiment and multi-payload verification, would follow. It provides no measured on-orbit 5G, AI-compute or communications performance; the launch and payload configuration are lab-reported claims.
